facts.statement: Tyrannoneustes lived during the Callovian stage in the Oxford Clay Formation of England and the Marnes de Dives of France.
facts.quote: Tyrannoneustes is an extinct genus of geosaurine metriorhynchid crocodyliform from the Callovian stage Oxford Clay Formation of England and the Marnes de Dives of France.

facts.statement: The only known species is Tyrannoneustes lythrodectikos, which translates to "blood-biting tyrant swimmer".
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Tyrannoneustes lythrodectikos, meaning "blood-biting tyrant swimmer".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Tyrannoneustes had a jaw that was 67 cm long.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen (CLAHM V972) had a 67 cm long jaw.

facts.statement: Other known individuals of Tyrannoneustes had skulls and jaws reaching approximately 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: while others known individuals were larger, with skull and jaws around the 1 m mark in length.

facts.statement: Tyrannoneustes belongs to the metriorhynchid subfamily Geosaurinae and the tribe Geosaurini.
facts.quote: Tyrannoneustes is a member of the metriorhynchid subfamily called Geosaurinae and the derived tribe Geosaurini.

facts.statement: Tyrannoneustes had a lower jaw measuring about 66 cm in length and possessed knife-like teeth.
facts.quote: Su mandíbula inferior medía cerca de 66 centímetros de largo y poseía dientes similares a cuchillos

facts.statement: Tyrannoneustes lived from the Callovian to the Oxfordian stages, between 165.3 and 159 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Oxfordian (165.3 to 159 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus was rediscovered in 2013 after being stored in a museum basement for a century following its discovery by Alfred Nicholson Leeds between 1907 and 1909.
rejected.quote: The genus was rediscovered after a century of storage in a museum basement after being unearthed by fossil hunter Alfred Nicholson Leeds between the years of 1907 and 1909.

rejected.statement: Tyrannoneustes had robust jaws and large, blade-like teeth adapted to attack prey as large or larger than itself.
rejected.quote: Its jaws were relatively robust and its teeth were large and blade-like, likely built to attack prey as large or larger than itself
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'to attack prey as large or larger than'
